extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for journal referees (and for editors to give referees) on producing consistently constructive, fair, and useful peer review comments for academic journal submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take steps to avoid decision fatigue
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that decision fatigue (a deterioration in decision-making quality from cumulative decisions) can lead to less articulate comments and missed critical points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work on peer reviews early in the day; do no more than one review at a time or within one sitting when possible; avoid reviewing when tired or hungry. Editors should remind reviewers to consider decision fatigue before accepting assignments because following these practices can produce higher-quality comments and faster reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cognizant of conscious and unconscious biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that both explicit conflicts of interest and implicit (unconscious) biases can cloud reviewers' judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have clear conflict of interest/competing interest policies (financial ties, academic commitments, personal relationships) and require disclosures. To curb implicit bias, consider double-anonymized peer review while acknowledging it may not fully prevent identity exposure. Remind reviewers to acknowledge everyone harbors implicit biases and provide actionable advice: 'focus on facts rather than feelings, slow down your decision making, and consider and reconsider the reasons for your conclusions' and 'root your review in evidence from the paper.' Offer unconscious bias prevention training or links to resources (e.g., recorded webinars).

rubrics_metrics.name: Null or negative results aren’t a basis for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'positive results bias' — do not favor manuscripts solely because their findings are positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make recommendations based on the quality of the research question, methodology, and perceived accuracy rather than the positivity of findings. Remind reviewers and editors that null and negative results can provide valuable or novel contributions and that rejecting on the basis of null/negative outcomes distorts the literature and creates inefficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: List the negatives and the positives
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should communicate both criticisms and strengths so authors know what to keep as well as what to improve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remind reviewers that the goal is to help authors identify what they are doing correctly as well as where to improve. Avoid overwhelmingly negative or snarky comments that can make authors discard useful parts of their manuscript; sarcasm may nullify useful feedback in the eyes of the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give concrete examples and advice (within scope!)
rubrics_metrics.description: Back up criticisms with concrete examples and actionable suggestions rather than vague statements like 'needs work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommending additional references, data points, or experiments, ensure suggestions are within the journal's scope and the subject matter, and be confident you could do the same if you were the author. Advise reviewers to log reactions and responses as they read to avoid blanket criticisms and to better notice positives. Provide real-world peer review examples (e.g., F1000 examples) and give reviewers detailed feedback forms and manuscript assessment checklists to help them stay on track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t be afraid to seek support
rubrics_metrics.description: It's acceptable for reviewers—especially early-career researchers—to seek mentorship or assistance when preparing reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage journals to help reviewers identify mentorship opportunities, offer peer reviewer training or links to resources (e.g., courses, guides), and allow co-reviewing with a mentor while keeping manuscript information confidential. For highly specialized matters, remind reviewers they can suggest bringing in an expert or request editorial assistance to obtain expert opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the Golden Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat authors' work as you would want your own to be treated: produce a thorough, fair review that you'd be satisfied to receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After completing a review, ask yourself if you would be satisfied with the quality had you received the same for your own work; if not, revise. Use this as a barometer for fairness and thoroughness.
